'''Hidegorō Nakano''' ({{langx|ja|中野 秀五郎}}; 16 May 1909 – 11 March 1974) is a Japanese mathematician,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hidegoro Nakano |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q95250078 |access-date=2022-06-21 |website=Wikidata|language=en}}{{user-generated source|date=July 2022}}</ref> after whom Nakano Spaces are named.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yamamuro |first=Sadayuki |title=ON CONJUGATE SPACES OF NAKANO SPACES |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1959-090-02/S0002-9947-1959-0132378-1/S0002-9947-1959-0132378-1.pdf |access-date=July 10, 2023|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>

== Life ==
Nakano was born as the first son of Katsugoro Nakano and Kame Nakano, in Tokyo. After graduating from National First High School, a preparatory school for the [[Imperial University of Tokyo]], he progressed to study mathematics in Tokyo Imperial University and graduated with a Bachelor of Science in 1933. Then he entered Graduate School at the same university under the supervision of Takuji Yoshie, and attained his doctoral degree in 1935. At that time, a doctorate was more commonly awarded to people over 50 years old.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hidegoro Nakano (1909â"1974) â" on the centenary of his birth 1 ... |url=https://moam.info/hidegoro-nakano-1909a1974-a-on-the-centenary-of-his-birth-1-_5a3bf6531723dd59d6715a5f.html |access-date=2022-06-22 |website=moam.info |language=en}}</ref>

Nakano started teaching in The National First High School in 1935. At the same year he married Sumiko Yamamura (11 December 1913, Tokyo - 5 March 1999, Detroit). Then he held academic positions (1938-1952) in Tokyo Imperial University, before moving to [[Hokkaido University]] and being appointed as a professor.<ref name=":1" />
 
In 1960, he left Japan and took a visit to [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in Canada for a year, under the invitation of [[Canadian Mathematical Congress]]. He then took up professorship in [[Wayne State University]], Detroit, US, in 1961, and continued working there until his death in 1974.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Hidegorō Nakano - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Nakano/ |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

== Works ==

=== Nakano's name in mathematics ===
Nakano is known for his research in [[Functional analysis|Functional Analysis]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=MR: Nakano, Hidegorō - 506533 |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/506533 |access-date=2022-06-21 |website=MathSciNet}}</ref>{{original research inline|date=July 2022}} especially in [[vector lattice]] and operator theory in [[Hilbert space]]s. He mainly made his name in his contribution to several mathematical subjects around [[Modular form|modulars]], [[Riesz space]]s, Orlicz-Nakano spaces and Nakano space.<ref name=":0" />
